dedupe_keys.name: real life or scheduling data at uzgent march to august 2021 operating room and surgeon scheduling instances

description: This data set gives realistic weekly planning problems for the operating rooms of Ghent University Hospital in Belgium, with the best schedules found by an exact optimisation algorithm. The producers are Babak Akbarzadeh and co-authors, who built the instances from interviews with the staff who compose operating room schedules and from the hospital's operating room logbook for 2021. Coverage is 24 weekly instances from March to August 2021: medium instances with 50 to 80 patients and large ones with 100 to 160, each with patients, surgeons, rooms, days and the master surgery schedule that allocates room time to specialties. For each instance the set includes the solution of the authors' branch-cut-and-price algorithm, which sequences surgeons across rooms and days to maximise the priority of the patients treated. The files are available as free XML downloads from Mendeley Data under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: the XML structure is documented only briefly, the data describe one hospital's elective surgery, and emergency cases and disruptions are not modelled. Simulation uses: benchmarking surgery scheduling methods, testing how losing rooms or staff during a crisis reduces elective capacity, and building hospital capacity models from realistic case mixes. Related records: patientflow (model-patientflow) addresses bed demand, and the radiology workflow simulation data (data-radiology-workflow-simulation-synthetic) cover imaging capacity.
